title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, how-tos, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:

This document is the canonical platform engineering reference for Redwood Inference's platform systems and services. It consolidates the current inventory of platform services, recommended dashboards and alerts, runbook procedures for high-severity incidents, common how-tos for platform engineers, an incident retrospective pattern summary, and the 12-month roadmap for the platform team. The goal is to provide on-call engineers and platform contributors a single, actionable reference that ties monitoring, operational playbooks, and delivery plans together.

Scope:
- Applies to services owned by the Platform team (k8s control plane integrations, shared infra services, internal APIs, observability stack, batch workers, and CI runners).
- Does NOT cover customer-facing product runtime SLAs (see eng-sre docs) or Dedicated customer on-prem package runbooks (see eng-private-deployments).

Ownership and Contacts:
- Platform owner: Priya Desai (platform lead)
- Observability owner: Marcus Liu (metrics & dashboards)
- Oncall rotation: platform@redwood-team (PagerDuty)
- Emergency escalation: Engineering Manager on call -> VP Eng (if not resolved within escalation window)

Systems & Services Inventory (high level):
| Service | Responsible | Primary metrics | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| platform-api (internal) | platform-service-team | latency_p50, latency_p95, error_rate | Serves internal control-plane requests; low-latency target 100ms p95
| observability-ingest | observability-team | incoming_lines, write_errors, cpu_usage | Accepts logs/metrics/traces; has backpressure queueing
| shared-cache (redis-cluster) | infra-team | cache_hit_rate, evictions, memory_used | Used for prefix/KV caching for inference; multi-az
| build-runners (k8s) | ci-team | queue_length, pod_startup_time, pod_failure_rate | Autoscaled by queue length; common source of latency for infra changes

Dashboards & Alerting Strategy:
- Dashboard tiers: Executive (SLO summary), Ops (service health), Debug (per-endpoint/host traces).
- Every service must have: 1) Health dashboard (errors, latency, traffic), 2) Infra dashboard (CPU/memory/disk/io), 3) Dependency map (calls to critical services).
- Alerting policy: prefer actionable alerts with runbook links. Alerts must include runbook link, pager escalation, and remediation hints.

Recommended dashboards (examples):
1) platform-service-health
   - Widgets: per-endpoint p95 latency, error rate (5m), requests/sec, recent traces (sampled).
   - SLOs: 99.9% availability (5xx rate < 0.1% over 7d).
2) observability-ingest-health
   - Widgets: incoming events/sec, write_errors (rate), queue_depth, retention_pressure
3) shared-cache-overview
   - Widgets: hit_rate, evictions, memory_by_node, replication_lag

Alert thresholds (platform defaults):
| Alert name | Condition | Severity | Pager? | Runbook |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| platform-api-high-error-rate | error_rate > 0.5% for 3m | P1 | yes | runbooks/platform-api-error-rate |
| platform-api-latency-degradation | p95_latency > 500ms for 5m | P1 | yes | runbooks/platform-api-latency |
| observability-ingest-backpressure | queue_depth > 10000 for 2m OR write_errors > 0.1% | P1 | yes | runbooks/observability-ingest-backpressure |
| shared-cache-memory-pressure | used_memory > 85% for 5m | P2 | no (Slack) | runbooks/redis-memory-pressure |

Runbooks (anchor, short summary + link pattern):
- runbooks/platform-api-error-rate:
  1) Confirm alert details (time window, affected endpoints).
  2) Check recent deployments (CI pipeline) and rollouts; if deployment in last 30 minutes, consider rollback or pause rollout.
  3) Inspect service logs (kubectl logs / centralized logging) and recent stack traces.
  4) Mitigation: enable traffic throttling, route to degraded instance pool, or fail open to a lower-cost path.
  5) If memory/CPU saturation detected, scale replicas and apply graceful restart.

- runbooks/observability-ingest-backpressure:
  1) Verify ingest cluster CPU and JVM metrics (or collector process metrics).
  2) If write_errors present, check Elasticsearch/TSDB availability and rate limits.
  3) Apply backpressure mitigation: increase ingest replicas, enable buffering on forwarders, temporarily drop non-essential logs.
  4) Notify downstream teams affected by delayed telemetry.

Detailed runbook example: platform-api-latency (quick-play):
- Trigger: p95 latency > 500ms for 5m
- Step 0: Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and add the alert link to the incident Slack channel #inc-platform-ops.
- Step 1: Run pre-defined queries:
  - kubectl top pods -n platform | sort -r -k3
  - curl -s 'https://grafana.internal/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))'
- Step 2: If a canary/rolling deployment is in progress, pause or rollback: see deploy tool docs at /confluence/eng-platform/deploy-tooling.
- Step 3: If saturation is host-level, scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=N
- Step 4: If no remediation, follow Escalation (page): contact SRE oncall -> engineering manager -> paging VP Eng.

How-tos (common operational recipes):
- Adding a new dashboard: 1) Fork dashboard template (dashboards/template.json), 2) Replace metric IDs with service-specific metrics, 3) Add annotations for recent deploys and runbook links, 4) Review with Marcus Liu and merge to grafana/dashboards repo.
- Creating an alert rule: 1) Use alert-template.yaml, 2) Set owner and escalation level, 3) Confirm runbook link is present (format: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/<slug>), 4) Submit PR and tag oncall reviewer.
- Onboarding a new service to platform SLOs: 1) Define SLI targets with product owner, 2) Implement telemetry, 3) Add to SLO dashboard and alert policy, 4) Run 30-day burn-in and review.

Retrospective & continuous improvement pattern (post-incident):
1) Timebox RCA summary draft within 72 hours of incident resolution.
2) Triage actions into: immediate (<=7d), medium (<=30d), long-term (>=30d).
3) Assign owners and include success criteria.
4) Track follow-ups in the platform backlog (label: postmortem-action).

Recent retrospective highlights (Q3 2026):
- Incident: observability-ingest backpressure (2026-08-12)
  - Root cause: broker configuration caused large batches to be retransmitted after partial failure.
  - Actions: improved client-side retry backoff, added queue_depth alert, increased observability-ingest replica HPA limits.
  - Measurable outcome: median ingest latency improved 45% over the next 30 days.

Roadmap (next 12 months, prioritized):
- Q4 2026: Shift-left dashboards (self-serve templates), automated dashboard PR generator, improve alert noise suppression (adaptive thresholds).
- Q1 2027: Service-level rollout of multi-az cache failover; GA of platform API per-endpoint SLOs.
- Q2 2027: Observability ingestion scaling refactor (move to shard-based ingestion), runbook automation (one-click mitigation playbooks).
- Q3 2027: Platform cost-visibility features (per-route cost dashboards), integration with Redwood Console billing signals.

Team wiki & documentation hygiene (guidelines):
- All runbooks must be owned and reviewed quarterly. Add "last_reviewed" date to the top of each runbook page.
- Use consistent naming: dash-<service>-health, runbook-<service>-<class>, alert-<service>-<condition>.
- Maintain a changelog header on dashboards and runbooks for significant edits.

Oncall handover checklist (3-5 minute procedure):
1) Review active alerts and their mute state.
2) Check ongoing incidents in #inc-platform-ops and update status.
3) Confirm pager rotation contact details and escalation path.
4) Validate critical dashboards are green (platform-service-health, observability-ingest-health, shared-cache-overview).

Appendix: Example alert rule (Prometheus-style YAML)

groups:
- name: platform.rules
  rules:
  - alert: PlatformApiHighErrorRate
    expr: rate(platform_api_http_errors_total[3m]) / rate(platform_api_http_requests_total[3m]) > 0.005
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
      team: platform
    annotations:
      summary: "High error rate for platform-api"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-api-error-rate"
